text.en:
Every day Pooja noted down the temperature, whether it rained, how windy it was and if the sky was cloudy.
"After a month," she said, "I can see how the weather changed day by day."

Weather is the condition of the atmosphere at a place at a particular time. Its elements are temperature, air pressure, wind, humidity, clouds and rainfall.
A thermometer measures temperature, a barometer measures air pressure, an anemometer measures wind speed, a rain gauge measures rainfall, and a hygrometer measures humidity. Humidity is the amount of water vapour in the air.
Weather changes from day to day, but the average weather of a place over many years is its climate. We use weather reports to plan travel, farming and safety.
Weather is the condition of the air at a place at a certain time.
Its elements are temperature, pressure, wind, humidity, clouds and rainfall.
Instruments such as a thermometer and a rain gauge measure them.
The average weather over many years is the climate.

problem.en: Which instrument would you use to measure rainfall?

text.en: Rainfall is the amount of water that falls.

why.en: We need to collect and measure it.

text.en: A rain gauge collects rain in a measured container.
So we use a rain gauge.

prompt.en: A friend says weather and climate mean the same thing. How will you explain?

requiredIdeas.en: Weather is today's condition; climate is the average over many years.
Weather changes daily; climate changes very slowly.

points.en: Weather is the condition of the air at a time and place.
Elements: temperature, pressure, wind, humidity, clouds and rainfall.
Climate is the average weather over many years.
